problem: The sentence 'The trade-off is more computation at render time, not more storage' overstates the case. For artwork with thousands of anchors (a detailed map or an illustration with heavy texture) the path data can be far bigger than a compressed raster of the same picture, so storage is sometimes a real cost.
fix: Rewrite: 'The trade-off is more computation at render time, and file size grows with the number of anchors; simple logos stay small, very detailed path artwork can be large.'

problem: The answer implies that filling requires the path to be closed. Most drawing software will fill an open path by treating it as if a straight line joined its two ends, so 'lets the interior be filled' is misleading as the main effect of closing.
fix: Answer: 'It joins the last anchor back to the first, so the outline has no ends. Strokes then show no endpoints, and the shape has an unambiguous inside; an open path can still be filled, but the software has to imagine the closing line itself.'

problem: 'Clicking with no drag gives a straight corner' is vague. A student may read 'straight corner' as a curve that happens to be straight, rather than a corner point that carries no handles.
fix: Write: 'Clicking with no drag places a corner point with no handles, so the segments on either side of it are straight lines.'
